subject: TLS keying material provenance + rotation sampling for SOC2 intake
messages:
From: Liam O'Connor <liam.o@archimedes-finance.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Cc: security@archimedes-finance.com
Date: Sat, 14 Nov 2026 08:15:00 -0800
Subject: SOC2 intake - TLS keying material and rotation sampling

Jonas,

Thanks for taking this. As part of our SOC2 readiness checklist we need the following from Redwood for the tenant environment that will host Archimedes data: a sampling of TLS keying metadata for the last 90 days (cipher suites used, cert thumbprints, key rollover timestamps), the HSM/KMS rotation logs that show key version changes and operator approvals, and your BYOK handover checklist for our archive. Our security team wants to cross-check provenance vs. the SCCM audit window next week.

Can you confirm what you can provide and an ETA? If you prefer a shared Drive folder we can use that; otherwise DocuSign for any acceptance statements is fine.

-Liam
Security, Archimedes Finance
liam.o@archimedes-finance.com

--
This message contains requests that may require export controls. Treat as confidential.

From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>

Date: Sun, 15 Nov 2026 09:04:00 -0800
Subject: Re: SOC2 intake - TLS keying material and rotation sampling

Thanks Liam — looping in Marissa and Kimberly (security engineering + product security) to coordinate the export. High level: we can supply a 90-day sampling window of TLS keying metadata (non-private elements only: cert thumbprints, algorithm, cipher suite, timestamps), a redacted operator-approved rotation log for the KMS/HSM operations, and our BYOK handover checklist.

Proposed delivery:
- Monday EOD PT: Drive folder with TLS metadata + CSV rotation export (redacted operator identifiers replaced with role tokens)
- Tuesday: BYOK handover checklist PDF and an abbreviated narrative describing rotation policy and retention windows

If Archimedes needs raw private key material we cannot provide that — BYOK handover contains wrapped key proofs and signing attestations instead. Confirm the Drive link preference and whether you need DocuSign on the checklist.

Jonas Weber
Security & Compliance Lead
Redwood Inference
jonas.weber@redwood.com

Hi Liam — attached is a compact delivery set per Jonas's timeline. Files uploaded to the shared Drive folder (link above) and also attached here as stubs: keystore-rotation-log.csv (rotation timestamps, wrapped-key-version, approval-role), tls-keying-metadata.jsonl (per-connection sample: date, ip-range, cert-thumbprint, cipher-suite, tls-version), byok-handover-checklist.pdf (handback steps and verification checklist).

Notes / caveats:
- We scrubbed direct operator IDs and replaced with role tokens (e.g., HSM_OP:S1) to preserve personnel privacy while showing approval flow. If you need operator-level audit extracts for a legal review we can provide them under an NDA amendment.
- The rotation CSV includes a 30-day clock skew correction used internally for cross-region alignment; we added a column "rotation_effective_utc" that you can use to correlate events.
- TLS metadata is sampled at 1% across ingress endpoints to preserve scale while providing representation of cipher mix. If you require full telemetry we will need a scheduled export and an allowance for increased egress.

Attachments (uploaded / attached):
- keystore-rotation-log.csv (attachment)
- tls-keying-metadata.jsonl (attachment)
- byok-handover-checklist.pdf (attachment)

Let us know if you want any additional columns in the CSV (operator_comment, roll_reason) and whether your auditors prefer the redaction as-is.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Senior Security Engineer, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com

Attachment stubs: [keystore-rotation-log.csv] (csv, 24KB), [tls-keying-metadata.jsonl] (jsonl, 48KB), [byok-handover-checklist.pdf] (pdf, 12 pages)
